title: Between Breathlessness and Anxiety: The Association Between Physical Symptom Burden and Psychological Well-Being in Patients Admitted to a Pulmonary Medicine Ward – A Prospective Longitudinal Observational Study
summary:
People with lung diseases often experience symptoms such as shortness of breath, cough, pain, or severe tiredness. These symptoms can affect not only everyday life and quality of life but may also be associated with anxiety and other forms of emotional distress.  At the same time, a person’s emotional well-being may influence how strongly physical symptoms are perceived.

The aim of this study is to investigate how physical symptoms, emotional well-being, and perceived quality of life are related in patients with lung diseases and how these factors change during a hospital stay. The study also aims to examine whether certain personal or social factors influence these relationships.

The study includes adult patients who are being treated on a hospital ward for lung diseases. Participants are asked about their physical symptoms, emotional well-being, and quality of life at the beginning of their hospital stay and again before discharge. Standardized questionnaires and rating scales are used for this purpose. In addition, selected personal information and information about the course of the illness are collected. Participation in the study does not involve any additional treatment or changes to the participants’ medical care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with a pulmonary disease admitted to a general hospital ward
- Written informed consent
- Sufficient language proficiency to understand and follow the instructions
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients unable to provide informed consent
- Patients with severe cognitive impairment
- Severe psychiatric disorders (psychosis, acute suicidality)
- Insufficient language proficiency
- Palliative care situation
- Participation in concurrent studies that may influence primary psychological outcomes
